title: Word 23 — On Malice
attribution_note: Word 23 of 28 in the collection Short Moral-Instructive Words — see Word 1 for provenance.

sections.heading: What malice is, and how it takes hold

pairs.en: Malice is anger grown hardened and old. Anger, if it is not soon subdued, turns into malice. This is why the apostle exhorts and teaches us to lay aside anger at its very onset: *“let not the sun go down upon your wrath; neither give place to the devil”* [Ephesians 4:26–27]. From this we see that whoever holds onto anger and malice against his neighbor gives place to the devil. Over such a man the devil, as the spirit of malice, has already gained mastery, and leads him about as his captive.

Malice is born either of envy — as Cain bore malice toward his brother Abel, envying his prosperity, and in his malice killed him [Genesis 4:8] — or of an injury done to a man. So people grow angry and malicious toward those who have wronged them, wishing to repay evil with evil, and thus to avenge their injury.

sections.heading: A vile passion that torments even the one who bears it

pairs.en: O fierce passion! Fierce and destructive both to those consumed by malice and to those against whom it rises up and arms itself. If it is not cut off at the start, it works great calamities, just as a fire, once it gathers strength, devours many houses. “Malice is such a thing that if a man does not cut it off at its very beginning, it multiplies without measure, like a fire that has found dry fuel,” says St. John Chrysostom.

sections.heading: The five ways malice does its work

pairs.en: 5) In some people malice works and multiplies so violently that they are not afraid to say: “I don't care if I destroy myself, so long as I get him!”

sections.heading: The wretchedness of such a soul

pairs.en: O poor creature! Do you not know what ruin is? Put your hand into a fire and you will taste a little of its bitterness. If you cannot bear even that, will you endure the bitterness of the fire of Gehenna, into which a man will be wholly plunged and submerged, and will burn and never be consumed, forever? But when you come to yourself, you will know that it is the devil, the spirit of malice, who produces and utters such words within you.

sections.heading: The bitter fruit malice leaves for all, and worst for the malicious themselves

pairs.en: See, beloved Christians, what a fierce and grievous evil malice is. Evil and bitter are the fruits of malice; evil and bitter is malice itself, which bears such fruits. Woe to the world because of malice! It harms everyone in every way, as has been said above, and from it no one, nowhere, can hide. When it cannot harm a man by other means, it releases its poison upon him through the tongue. Whatever calamities, misfortunes, and evils exist in the world, malice is the cause of them all. So then, woe to the world because of malice! But greater woe still to the malicious themselves! They harm the bodies of others, and their own souls; they put to death the bodies of others, and their own souls; they take away the temporal life of others, and their own eternal life; they destroy others only for a time, but destroy themselves forever. To such grievous evil does malice lead.

sections.heading: The remedy: two reasons to lay malice down

pairs.en: 2) It often happens that the malicious, wishing to harm others, first harm themselves: the poison they prepare for others they themselves swallow; with the sword they draw against others they slay themselves, and their sword enters into their own hearts [Psalm 36:15]; and into the pit they dig for others they themselves fall. This is what the Psalmist sings of: *“He hath made a pit, and digged it, and is fallen into the ditch which he made.* *His mischief shall return upon his own head, and his violent dealing shall come down upon his own pate”* [Psalm 7:15–16]. And the Lord says: *“with what measure ye mete, it shall be measured to you again”* [Matthew 7:2].

Beloved Christians! Let us heed the apostolic exhortation: *“let not the sun go down upon your wrath,”* and let us subdue and tame anger at its very onset, and while this lawless infant is still small, let us kill it, lest it grow and master us. Laying aside all malice and all guile, and hypocrisy, and envy, and all evil speaking, let us, as newborn babes, desire the pure milk of the word, that we may grow thereby unto salvation [1 Peter 2:1–2]. *“Beloved, follow not that which is evil, but that which is good.* *He that doeth good is of God: but he that doeth evil hath not seen God”* [3 John 1:11]. Amen.
